ex: Hon har alltid varit intresserad av {konst}.
exEn: She has always been interested in art.
note: Det är ingen konst! = It's easy, there's nothing to it. A painter or sculptor is en konstnär.

ex: Den här {målningen} är över hundra år gammal.
exEn: This painting is over a hundred years old.
note: A painting on the wall is often just called en tavla.

ex: Det här är museets mest kända {konstverk}.
exEn: This is the museum's most famous work of art.
note: Same form in the plural: ett konstverk, två konstverk.

ex: Museet har en ny {utställning} om vikingatiden.
exEn: The museum has a new exhibition about the Viking Age.

ex: Jag vill ha ett mer {kreativt} jobb.
exEn: I want a more creative job.
note: Stress on the last syllable: kre-a-TIV.

ex: Vilken sorts {musik} gillar du?
exEn: What kind of music do you like?
note: Stress on the second syllable: mu-SIK.

ex: Jag älskar den här {låten}!
exEn: I love this song!
note: The everyday word for a song or track. Also the imperative of låta: Låt mig! = Let me!

ex: Vi sjöng en {sång} för mormor.
exEn: We sang a song for Grandma.
note: Also singing: Hon studerar sång. For a pop song or track, låt is more common.

ex: Han är {sångare} i ett rockband.
exEn: He's a singer in a rock band.
note: A female singer is often called en sångerska.

ex: Vilken {artist} lyssnar du mest på?
exEn: Which artist do you listen to the most?
note: False friend: en artist is a performer, like a singer. A painter is en konstnär.

ex: Hon jobbar som {musiker} i Stockholm.
exEn: She works as a musician in Stockholm.
note: Same form in the plural: en musiker, två musiker.

ex: Vi startade ett {band} när vi gick i skolan.
exEn: We started a band when we were in school.
note: Same form in the plural: ett band, två band.

ex: Min mamma sjunger i {kör} varje torsdag.
exEn: My mom sings in a choir every Thursday.
note: Hard k here, unlike kör (drive!) from köra, which starts with the tj-sound.

ex: Vi ska gå på {konsert} i helgen.
exEn: We're going to a concert this weekend.
note: The t is silent in konsert ('kon-SÄR'), but you hear it in konserten.

ex: Spelar du något {instrument}?
exEn: Do you play an instrument?

ex: Jag har spelat {gitarr} i fem år.
exEn: I've been playing the guitar for five years.
note: The g is soft: 'yi-TARR'. No article: spela gitarr = play the guitar.

ex: Min son vill lära sig spela {piano}.
exEn: My son wants to learn to play the piano.

ex: Grannens son spelar {trummor} hela dagarna.
exEn: The neighbor's son plays the drums all day long.
note: To play the drums = spela trummor (plural, no article).

ex: Min dotter spelar {fiol} i skolans orkester.
exEn: My daughter plays the violin in the school orchestra.
note: En violin also exists, but fiol is the everyday word.

ex: Bandet ska {spela in} ett nytt album i vår.
exEn: The band is going to record a new album this spring.
note: Particle verb: the stress is on in. A recording is en inspelning.

ex: Kan du sänka {ljudet} lite?
exEn: Can you turn the sound down a bit?
note: lj is pronounced j: 'yood'.

ex: Ska vi se en {film} i kväll?
exEn: Shall we watch a movie tonight?
note: Watch a movie = se (or titta på) en film.

ex: Jag har börjat titta på en ny {serie}.
exEn: I've started watching a new series.
note: Also a comic strip. A comic book is en serietidning.

ex: Vi såg tre {avsnitt} på en kväll.
exEn: We watched three episodes in one evening.
note: Same form in the plural: ett avsnitt, tre avsnitt.

ex: Hon drömmer om att bli {skådespelare}.
exEn: She dreams of becoming an actor.
note: Used for both men and women. Skådespelerska (actress) also exists.

ex: Filmens {regissör} kommer från Göteborg.
exEn: The movie's director is from Gothenburg.
note: The g is pronounced with the sj-sound: 're-shi-SÖR'.

ex: Han fick en liten {roll} i filmen.
exEn: He got a small part in the movie.
note: Det spelar ingen roll = It doesn't matter.

ex: Jag såg en {kändis} på tåget i morse.
exEn: I saw a celebrity on the train this morning.
note: From känd (famous). The k is soft: tj-sound.

ex: Vi såg en {pjäs} av Strindberg.
exEn: We saw a play by Strindberg.

ex: {Föreställningen} börjar klockan sju.
exEn: The show starts at seven.

ex: Bandet gick upp på {scenen} klockan nio.
exEn: The band went on stage at nine o'clock.
note: sc is pronounced s. Also a scene in a movie or play.

ex: {Publiken} klappade i händerna och sjöng med.
exEn: The audience clapped and sang along.
note: False friend: publik means audience. 'The public' is allmänheten.

ex: Ge henne en stor {applåd}!
exEn: Give her a big round of applause!
note: Often in the plural: långa applåder. To applaud = applådera.

ex: Vad blir det på {tv} i kväll?
exEn: What's on TV tonight?
note: Pronounced 'teve'. Watch TV = titta på tv. The plural is usually tv-apparater (TV sets).

ex: Jag lyssnar på {radio} i bilen.
exEn: I listen to the radio in the car.
note: No article: lyssna på radio. The plural is usually radioapparater (radio sets).

ex: Vilket {program} tittar du på?
exEn: Which show are you watching?
note: Double m in the definite forms: programmet, programmen.

ex: Det är så mycket {reklam} på tv nu.
exEn: There are so many ads on TV these days.
note: Uncountable. A single TV ad is en reklamfilm; an ad in print is en annons.

ex: Jag lyssnar på {poddar} när jag tränar.
exEn: I listen to podcasts when I work out.
note: Also called en podcast.

ex: Filmen fick bra {recensioner}.
exEn: The movie got good reviews.
note: To review = recensera.

ex: Det blir mat, musik och {underhållning} hela kvällen.
exEn: There will be food, music and entertainment all evening.
note: From underhålla = to entertain.

ex: Hon skriver på sin första {roman}.
exEn: She's writing her first novel.
note: False friend: en roman is a novel, not a romance.

ex: Astrid Lindgren är en känd svensk {författare}.
exEn: Astrid Lindgren is a famous Swedish author.

ex: Boken bygger på en sann {berättelse}.
exEn: The book is based on a true story.
note: From berätta = to tell.

ex: Han skrev en {dikt} till sin fru.
exEn: He wrote a poem for his wife.
note: Poetry is poesi or lyrik.
